requirement: PWR shall supply the thruster strings from a 100 V regulated bus (TBC), delivering at least 25 kW at the PPU inputs at end of life through six individually protected and switchable feeds of at least 5 kW each.

interface: Refuelling (propellant module to DRI to PROP)
requirement: The xenon path from the DRI coupling to the PROP tanks shall carry at least 2,550 kg per refuelling within 21 days (an average of about 121 kg/day), with an isolation valve on each side of the DRI-PROP interface (leak rate TBD).
TCS shall remove up to 1.25 kW of PPU waste heat from the PROP thermal interface at the design point, and up to 3.3 kW in total in Transfer (interface temperatures TBD).

Each thruster string (PPU, thruster and flow control) shall connect to the rest of the tug only through its power feed, its xenon feed and the on-board data bus, so that strings, or a whole propulsion module, can later be exchanged without changing other components.
CDH, GNC, PROP, PWR, DRI and COMMS shall exchange commands and status over a redundant on-board data bus (standard chosen in the physical architecture).
COMMS shall receive approach clearance from the lunar orbit destination over a proximity radio link (band TBC, range TBD) and pass it to GNC through CDH within TBD s.
STR shall provide a launch adapter interface compatible with Ariane 64 for a tug launch mass of up to 11,500 kg (adapter type TBD from the Ariane 6 user's manual).

The propulsion module shall connect to the tug through one mechanical latch, one power connector rated for 25 kW at 100 V (TBC), one xenon feed coupling and one data connector, all mated and demated in orbit (number of cycles TBD).
